items.title: Work Done
items.body: \(W=Fd\cos\theta\) where \(F\) is force, \(d\) distance, \(\theta\) angle between force and displacement. Units: Joules (J).

items.title: Potential Energy
items.body: Gravitational PE: \(GPE=mgh\). Change in GPE: \(\Delta GPE=mg\Delta h\).

items.title: Power
items.body: \(P=\dfrac{W}{t}=Fv\). Units: Watts (W). Maximum speed when driving force = resistance: \(P=F_{resistance}\cdot v_{max}\).

body.en: Kinetic energy: \(\text{KE}=\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2\). Gravitational PE: \(\text{GPE}=mgh\). Work-energy principle: net work done = change in KE. Work done by a force: \(W=Fd\cos\theta\). Power: \(P=\dfrac{W}{t}=Fv\). Conservation of energy: \(\text{KE}_1+\text{GPE}_1=\text{KE}_2+\text{GPE}_2\) (no friction).

label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Energy, Work & Power

body.en: Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5), multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.

body.en:
Double-counting gravity: In energy equations, you either account for gravity through Gravitational Potential Energy (\(\Delta KE + \Delta PE = W_{\text{external}}\)) OR through work done by gravity (\(\Delta KE = W_g + W_{\text{friction}} + \dots\)). Including both simultaneously counts gravitational work twice.

Driving force vs Net force in \(P = Fv\): The force in \(P = Fv\) is the tractive/driving force produced by the engine, NOT the resultant force. At maximum or steady velocity, acceleration is zero, so the driving force exactly equals the total opposing resistance (\(F_{\text{drive}} = R + mg\sin\alpha\)).

Work against friction: Work done against friction is \(W = F \times d\) (where \(d\) is the distance along the surface). This mechanical energy converts irreversibly into heat.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Energy, Work & Power)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

A 2 kg ball rolls down a smooth slope of height 5 m from rest. Find its speed at the bottom (\(g=10\) m/s²).

\[\text{Loss in GPE}=\text{Gain in KE}:\quad2\times10\times5=\tfrac{1}{2}\times2\times v^2\Rightarrow v^2=100\Rightarrow v=10\text{ m/s}.\]

A car of mass 900 kg moves at constant speed 30 m/s against a resistance of 500 N. Find the power output of the engine.

At constant speed, driving force = resistance = 500 N.

\[P=Fv=500\times30=15\,000\text{ W}=15\text{ kW}.\]

body.en:
Problem (Medium): The point \( (-3,-6) \) lies on the curve \( y=f(x) \). Find the coordinates of the corresponding point on \( y=2f(x) \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Since the output is scaled by a factor of 2, the image point is \( (-3,-12) \).

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Energy, Work & Power (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): The curve \( y=x^2 \) is stretched parallel to the y-axis with scale factor 2, then translated by \( \begin{pmatrix}7\\-4\end{pmatrix} \). State the coordinates of the new vertex.

Step-by-Step Solution: A stretch parallel to the y-axis does not move the vertex \((0,0)\); the translation then moves it to \( (7,-4) \).

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Energy, Work & Power)

rows.en: The \(25\%\) reduction applies to the larger base \(1.25 Q_0\), not \(Q_0\).
Dividing by a negative number reverses order on the real number line.
Flip the inequality symbol whenever multiplying or dividing by a negative: \(x < -4\).
Computing round-trip average speed as \(\frac{v_1 + v_2}{2}\)
Time spent at the slower speed is longer than time spent at the faster speed.
Use total distance over total time: \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Energy, Work & Power

body.en: High-Speed Exam Shortcut (Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5)): When a linear system asks for a combined expression like \(3x + 3y\) rather than \(x\) and \(y\) individually, add or subtract the two equations directly before isolating either variable—this often yields the target expression in a single step.

question.en: A car of mass \(1200\text{ kg}\) ascends a hill of inclination \(\alpha\), where \(\sin\alpha = \tfrac{1}{20}\), against a constant resistance to motion of \(500\text{ N}\). Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\): (a) find the driving force required to travel at a steady speed of \(25\text{ m/s}\), (b) calculate the power developed by the engine in kilowatts.

solution.en: (a) Component of weight down the slope: \[W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\alpha = 1200(9.8)\left(\tfrac{1}{20}\right) = 60(9.8) = 588\text{ N}\] Since the car travels at steady speed (acceleration \(a = 0\)), the engine driving force balances all resistance: \[F_{\text{drive}} = \text{Resistance} + mg\sin\alpha = 500 + 588 = 1088\text{ N}\] (b) Power output: \[P = F_{\text{drive}} \times v = 1088 \times 25 = 27\,200\text{ W} = 27.2\text{ kW}\]

Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Isolate the primary variable or parameter systematically and simplify like terms before substituting numerical values.
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en: A block of mass \(5\text{ kg}\) is released from rest at the top of a rough plane inclined at \(30^\circ\) to the horizontal. The length of the incline is \(8\text{ m}\) and the coefficient of friction is \(\mu = 0.2\). Using the work-energy principle and taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\), calculate the speed of the block at the bottom of the incline.

solution.en:
1. Vertical height descended: \(h = 8\sin 30^\circ = 8(0.5) = 4\text{ m}\).
Initial gravitational potential energy: \[\text{PE} = mgh = 5(9.8)(4) = 196\text{ J}\] 2. Normal reaction: \(R = mg\cos 30^\circ = 5(9.8)\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 24.5\sqrt{3}\text{ N}\).
Friction force: \(F = \mu R = 0.2(24.5\sqrt{3}) = 4.9\sqrt{3}\text{ N}\).
Work done against friction over distance \(d = 8\text{ m}\): \[W_{\text{fric}} = F \times d = (4.9\sqrt{3}) \times 8 = 39.2\sqrt{3} \approx 67.896\text{ J}\] 3. By work-energy principle: \[\text{Gain in KE} = \text{Loss in PE} - W_{\text{fric}} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = 196 - 67.896 = 128.104\text{ J}\] Substitute \(m = 5\text{ kg}\): \[2.5v^2 = 128.104 \Rightarrow v^2 = \dfrac{128.104}{2.5} = 51.2416 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{51.2416} \approx 7.16\text{ m/s (3 s.f.)}\]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Energy, Work & Power and start from \(5\text{ kg}\).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(h = 8\sin 30^\circ = 8(0.5) = 4\text{ m}\).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en: [Practice 3 · Easy] A constant force of 15 N is applied to an object, causing it to move a distance of 4 m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done by the force.

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the mathematical relationship in Energy, Work & Power and write down the given values.
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Substitute the known quantities into the governing equation or formula and simplify step by step.
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Verify that your final result satisfies all conditions stated in the problem.

solution.en:
The work done by a constant force is given by the formula:
Work Done = Force × Distance × cos(θ)
where θ is the angle between the force and the direction of motion.
In this case, the force and the distance are in the same direction, so θ = 0°.
Therefore, cos(0°) = 1.
Work Done = 15 N × 4 m × 1
Work Done = 60 J
